import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Mahler's 3/2 Problem

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahler%27s_3/2_problem)
-/

namespace Mahler32

/-- For a real number `α`, define `Ω(α)` as
$$
\Omega (\alpha )=\inf _{\theta > 0}\left({\limsup _{n\rightarrow \infty }\left\lbrace
{\theta \alpha ^{n}}\right\rbrace -\liminf _{n\rightarrow \infty }\left\lbrace {\theta \alpha ^{n}}\right\rbrace }\right).
$$
-/
noncomputable def Ω (α : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  sInf {Filter.atTop.limsup (fun n ↦ Int.fract (θ * α ^ n))
    - Filter.atTop.liminf (fun n ↦ Int.fract (θ * α ^ n)) | (θ : ℝ) (_ : 0 < θ)}

/-- The **Mahler Conjecture** states that there are no Z-numbers. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem mahler_conjecture (x : ℝ) (hx : IsZNumber x) : False := by
  sorry

/-- If Mahler's conjecture is true, i.e. there are no Z-numbers, then `Ω(3/2)` exceeds `1/2`. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem mahler_conjecture.variants.consequence (H : type_of% mahler_conjecture) :
    1 / 2 < Ω (3 / 2) := by
  sorry

/-- It is known that for all rational `p/q > 1` in lowest terms, we have `Ω(p/q) > 1/p`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem mahler_conjecture.variants.flatto_lagarias_pollington (p q : ℕ) (hq : 1 < q)
    (hpq : p.Coprime q) (hpq' : q < p) : 1 / p < Ω (p / q) := by
  sorry

end Mahler32

findings.description: The implication is reversed. Lean assumes `∀ x : ℝ, IsZNumber x → False` and concludes `1 / 2 < Ω (3 / 2)`. The cited source instead gives the oscillation bound as a sufficient condition for the nonexistence of Z-numbers. This is a converse, not a contrapositive. A Z-number supplies a sequence with limsup at most 1/2 and liminf at least 0, hence Ω(3/2) ≤ 1/2; that argument establishes the source's direction. I proved that direction independently in Lean without using any sorry-backed theorem.
findings.source_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahler%27s_3/2_problem: “Mahler's conjecture would follow if Ω(3/2) exceeds 1/2.”
findings.suggested_fix: Reverse the hypothesis and conclusion: `theorem mahler_conjecture.variants.consequence (hΩ : 1 / 2 < Ω (3 / 2)) : type_of% mahler_conjecture := by sorry`. Update the docstring to say that the bound implies Mahler's conjecture.

findings.description: The strict inequality `1 / p < Ω (p / q)` strengthens the cited FLP theorem, which gives only `1 / p ≤ Ω (p / q)`. Since Ω is an infimum over all positive θ, the Lean statement requires a positive uniform gap above 1/p, rather than merely the stated lower bound. The primary theorem does not exclude the infimum being exactly 1/p. Wikipedia also displays the strict sign, so this appears to propagate an error in the encyclopedic source rather than faithfully state FLP's result.
findings.source_evidence: Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington, “On the range of fractional parts {ξ(p/q)^n}”, Acta Arithmetica 70 (1995), Theorem 1.4, p. 129, states limsup − liminf ≥ 1/p for every ξ > 0 and coprime p > q ≥ 2. Page 130 explicitly says: “In comparison Theorem 1.4 asserts that Ω(p/q) ≥ 1/p.” https://doi.org/10.4064/aa-70-2-125-147 ; https://www.impan.pl/shop/publication/transaction/download/product/108521?download.pdf
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the conclusion with `1 / p ≤ Ω (p / q)` and change the docstring's inequality accordingly. Cite Theorem 1.4 of the primary paper directly.

findings.description: Independently of the inequality issue, the docstring says “for all rational p/q > 1 in lowest terms,” whereas the Lean statement correctly requires `1 < q`. The prose therefore includes integers, for which the asserted positive lower bound is false: p = 2, q = 1 gives Ω(2) = 0, since θ = 1 makes every fractional part zero. I verified Ω(k) = 0 for natural-number k in Lean. The denominator restriction should remain in the statement.
findings.source_evidence: FLP (1995), p. 126: “We exclusively consider the case of (non-integer) rationals θ = p/q, where p > q ≥ 2 are relatively prime.” Theorem 1.4 repeats these hypotheses. https://doi.org/10.4064/aa-70-2-125-147
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the docstring with “non-integer rational p/q > 1,” or explicitly state that p > q ≥ 2 are coprime.

reformulations.difference: The imported `IsZNumber` requires the fractional-part condition for n ≥ 1, agreeing with Wikipedia, while Mahler's original paper imposes it for n ≥ 0. The nonexistence statement is nevertheless equivalent.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any positive number satisfying the original n ≥ 0 condition also satisfies the Lean n ≥ 1 condition. Conversely, from a Lean Z-number x, take y = x·(3/2). For every natural n, y·(3/2)^n = x·(3/2)^(n+1), so y satisfies the original condition, including n = 0. Fractional-part nonnegativity is automatic. Thus existence, and therefore nonexistence, is unchanged. The exact equivalence between the Lean theorem's type and nonexistence under the original definition was proved in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`.

sources_consulted: K. Mahler, “An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2”, Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society 8 (1968), 313–321, especially p. 313 and the final remarks; https://doi.org/10.1017/S1446788700005371

L. Flatto, J. C. Lagarias and A. D. Pollington, “On the range of fractional parts {ξ(p/q)^n}”, Acta Arithmetica 70 (1995), 125–147, especially Theorem 1.4, pp. 129–130, its proof, and the final remarks; https://www.impan.pl/shop/publication/transaction/download/product/108521?download.pdf

Y. Bugeaud, “Linear mod one transformations and the distribution of fractional parts {ξ(p/q)^n}”, Acta Arithmetica 114 (2004), 301–311, introduction and main results; https://irma.math.unistra.fr/~bugeaud/travaux/AA3883.pdf

Y. Bugeaud and A. Dubickas, “Fractional parts of powers and Sturmian words”, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 341 (2005), 69–74, introduction and statement of the FLP bound; https://irma.math.unistra.fr/~bugeaud/travaux/BugeDubCRAS.pdf
https://irma.math.unistra.fr/~bugeaud/Book2.html (book information page, not the book text)
review.notes: Checked all four declarations. The definition of Ω is faithful: its exponent index is ℕ, its θ-domain is nonempty, and its oscillations lie in [0,1], so real infimum/limsup/liminf default cases do not arise. Independent Lean checks proved 0 ≤ Ω(α) ≤ 1, Ω(k) = 0 for natural k, the source's implication, and the reindexing equivalence. `/workspace/review/infimum_checks.lean` also proves that c ≤ Ω(α) is equivalent to the corresponding pointwise non-strict lower bound for every positive θ. These proofs have no sorryAx dependency. Positivity, strict fractional-part endpoints, rational coercions, and the smallest admissible pair (p,q) = (3,2) were checked. No answer slots or formal_proof attributes occur. The target file's hash matches the specified commit.

not_demonstrated.reason: The earlier scratch proof establishes the source's implication, not the converse stated here or its negation. Proving the opposite implication does not refute this declaration. A disproof would require both establishing the nonexistence of Z-numbers and showing Ω(3/2) ≤ 1/2; no short proof of these is available.

The source's non-strict lower bound does not disprove the strict bound. No admissible coprime p > q ≥ 2 with Ω(p/q) ≤ 1/p has been established. The scratch computation Ω(2) = 0 uses q = 1, which the actual declaration excludes, so it is not a counterexample.

submission.summary: The reported source discrepancies do not provide trivial proofs or disproofs of these exact Lean statements. No trivial_proof.lean was created, and no compilation of that file was attempted.
submission.gave_up_reason: Neither reported misformalization has a short, honest demonstration of the required kind available. Presenting the corrected implication, weakening the inequality, dropping the denominator hypothesis, or invoking the imported admitted theorems would not demonstrate the declarations as stated.

submission.summary: Reversed the conditional variant so that Ω(3/2) > 1/2 implies the nonexistence of Z-numbers. Changed the FLP lower bound from strict to non-strict, clarified the coprime p > q ≥ 2 restriction in its docstring, and cited the primary paper's Theorem 1.4 directly. The edited file compiles with only the expected `sorry` warnings.
